newsitem.title: UK: Britain's MOD orders 1,000 missiles from Shorts.
newsitem.headline: Britain's MOD orders 1,000 missiles from Shorts.

text.p: Shorts Missile Systems Ltd (SMS) said on Monday that Britain's Defence Ministry had signed a contract for an additional 1,000 Starstreak missiles.
This brings the total number of missiles in service with the British army to more than 7,000, SMS said in a statement.
SMS is a joint venture between Belfast-based Shorts Brothers Plc, a subsidiary of Canada's Bombardier Inc, and Thomson-CSF of France.
"Starstreak's important role with the British Army is once again confirmed by this latest order which I welcome," SMS chairman Roy McNulty said.
"The system's capability is unparalleled in the close air defence systems markets and this obviously bodes well for the future," McNulty, who is attending the Paris Air Show, said in the statement.

He also said that Bombardier Aerospace's' aerostructures and nacelles programmes had expanded significantly at Shorts, helping the Northern Irish company to recover quickly following the collapse of Fokker in 1996.
The break-up of Fokker meant Shorts lost some 17 percent of its business and some 900 employees lost their jobs.
"This was a real setback but, in the short term, it has been partly offset by increased production rates on existing Bombardier aircraft programmes and on our nacelles and Boeing programmes."

McNulty said Shorts had started 10 new aerostructures or nacelle programmes in the past three years and these would account for almost 60 percent of its aerospace business at Belfast by the year 2000.

In the long term, the loss of the Fokker work would be more than replaced by Shorts participation in two new Bombardier aircraft programmes announced in January -- the Canadair Regional Jet Series 700 and the de Havilland Dash 8-400.
Shorts is part of the engineering team designing these aircraft and will play a significant role in their manufacture.
McNulty said up to 1,000 new jobs should be created over the next four to five years as a result of these new programmes.
